REST vs GraphQL Basics: storyboard

Episode 6 · voice Matilda · 9 scenes · 82.8s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Hook · 0.0s–7.6s

Headline: Replace? Not quite.

“GraphQL was supposed to replace REST. So why is REST still everywhere? Because they solve different problems.”

branding sting 7.6s–9.1s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Slider · 9.1s–18.0s

Headline: Menu or order

“REST is a set menu: every dish comes as listed. GraphQL is a custom order: you name exactly what you want.”

breakdown rest Snippet · 18.0s–28.4s

Headline: One address each

“In REST, every thing has its own address. Ask for a user and you get the whole user: name, email, bio, everything.”

breakdown gql Snippet · 28.4s–36.1s

No headline

“GraphQL has one address. You send a query naming only the fields you want, and the reply has exactly those.”

breakdown trips Sequence · 36.1s–47.3s

Headline: Too many trips

“The opposite problem is under-fetching. A profile screen needs a user, posts and comments: three trips on mobile data. GraphQL asks once.”

breakdown cache Split · 47.3s–57.2s

No headline

“Flexibility has a price. REST addresses are easy for a CDN to cache. One GraphQL address with changing queries is harder.”

breakdown nplus Sequence · 57.2s–65.6s

Headline: N plus one

“Then there's the N plus one problem. Load ten posts, then one author lookup per post: eleven database hits.”

breakdown rule Matrix · 65.6s–76.5s

Headline: Pick by need

“GitHub offers both. Simple, cacheable resources? REST. Many screens needing different data shapes? GraphQL.”

gist gist GistCard · 76.5s–82.8s

No headline

“That's the gist: REST is simple and cacheable, GraphQL is flexible. Follow for more.”
